# monitorable_servers (Data Source)

Lists the servers of the organization, optionally filtered by liveness status or a name fragment. Use it to find a server that exists but is not in Terraform state, for example after an interrupted apply, and adopt it with `terraform import`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Every server whose name contains "web" (case-insensitive) and that has not
# reported for a while.
data "monitorable_servers" "quiet_web" {
  name_contains = "web"
  status        = "offline"
}

output "quiet_web_ids" {
  value = [for s in data.monitorable_servers.quiet_web.servers : s.id]
}

# After an interrupted apply, find the server that was created but never made
# it into state, then adopt it with `terraform import monitorable_server.web <id>`.
data "monitorable_servers" "all" {}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `name_contains` (String) Only servers whose name contains this text; the match is case-insensitive. Omit for all names.
- `status` (String) Only servers with this liveness status: `online`, `stale`, `offline` or `dormant`. Omit for all statuses.

### Read-Only

- `servers` (Attributes List) The matching servers, ordered by id. Empty when none match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--servers))

<a id="nestedatt--servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `servers`

Read-Only:

- `agent_version` (String) The version of the agent running on the server. Empty until the agent first reports.
- `alert_template_id` (String) The id of the alert template assigned to the server, a decimal integer. `"0"` means the server follows the organization's default template.
- `alerts_muted` (Boolean) Whether alerts for the server are muted right now.
- `alerts_muted_until` (String) When the current mute ends (RFC 3339, UTC). Null when alerts are not muted.
- `country_code` (String) The two-letter country code of the server's location. Empty when unknown.
- `created_at` (String) When the server was created (RFC 3339, UTC).
- `created_via` (String) How the server was created, as the API reports it: for example `api` for a server created through the API or this provider, `dashboard` for one created in the dashboard.
- `id` (String) The server id, a decimal integer.
- `ip` (String) The address the agent last reported from. Empty until the agent first reports.
- `ipv4` (String) The IPv4 address the agent last reported from. Empty when there is none.
- `ipv6` (String) The IPv6 address the agent last reported from. Empty when there is none.
- `last_seen_at` (String) When the agent last reported (RFC 3339, UTC). Null if it never has.
- `location` (String) The server's location as the API reports it. Empty when unknown.
- `name` (String) The server's display name.
- `open_incidents` (Number) The number of open incidents on the server.
- `status` (String) Liveness: `online`, `stale`, `offline` or `dormant`. A server that has never reported is `offline` (`dormant` after seven days).
- `triage` (String) The dashboard's triage tier for the server, for example `healthy` or `unreachable`. A server that has never reported is `unreachable`.
- `unacked_firing` (Number) The number of firing incidents on the server that nobody has acknowledged.
- `uptime_seconds` (Number) The host's uptime in seconds as last reported; `0` until the agent first reports.
